title: Lawrence of Arabia
note: The best one to start with. It's an identity-dissolution film — the movie keeps asking Lawrence who he is and he loses the thread, suspended between two selves that are both performances. Same shape as The Prestige at desert scale. The risk is format, not content: composed for a screen the size of a building, with an intermission built in. Biggest screen available, one sitting.

title: Hour of the Wolf
note: Bergman doing outright horror. Short, direct, not asking to be admired — the exact profile that already earned two perfect scores.

title: After Hours
note: Old but fast and unhinged rather than stately. Scorsese in King of Comedy mode.

title: Possession
note: Old, and the opposite of slow. Closer to The Substance than to anything canonical.

title: Apocalypse Now
note: Genuinely about a man dissolving. But stately, and its reputation does a lot of the talking.

title: Stalker
note: Three men walking and talking. The purest version of the thing that doesn't land for you. Save it for after Lawrence.
